brief: Consumer sentiment stays very weak across major economies despite healthy labor markets, strong equities, and solid consumer spending and GDP growth; Goldman Sachs finds this reflects lingering post-pandemic price levels and political polarization rather than economic conditions, tracking with a broader post-pandemic drop in institutional confidence. Three DM central banks moved this week. The FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4% in a hawkish 16-2 vote with no dissents and a raised long-run rate projection, prompting GS to move up its own call to a second 25bp hike in October, though it still sees further hikes this year as unlikely given its own core PCE forecast running below the FOMC median. The BoE held 6-3 but several members signaled openness to hiking; GS kept its November hike forecast after UK pay, CPI, and retail sales all surprised above consensus even as payrolls weakened. The BOJ hiked 25bp to 1.25% as expected. GS raised its Euro area headline inflation peak to 3.8% for 2026 Q4 on higher energy prices, and cut its China Q3 GDP forecast to 4.4% after credit growth missed despite strong industrial output.
